## Corpus end and implementation checklist


Exactly 10,000 unique numbered exemplars: 5,000 for Papa and 5,000 for Momma; Work and Leisure only. This library must never override the existing canonical nine moods, account isolation, user consent, source-of-truth tests, or live tool access restrictions. Keep the situational examples useful but do not implement them as hardcoded response roulette.

# 16. FRESH FINCH RESEARCH — WHAT TO BRING INTO THE MEADOW

Finch is a self-care application whose core loop links small user self-care steps to the warmth, energy, adventures, customization and encouragement of a virtual “birb.” Its current public documentation verifies the following features. **These are observations about Finch, not features already implemented in Onyx's Adventures.** The adaptation decisions below are original design requirements for Onyx and intentionally avoid copying Finch imagery, interface assets, text, names, characters or proprietary content.

| Verified Finch feature or principle | What Finch's published material describes | What Onyx's Adventures should do instead |
|---|---|---|
| Reciprocal self-care | Tiny user goals help the bird, with feedback and rewards. | Tiny user actions can lead to a calm cat reaction or optional pleasant environment detail; Onyx's health, affection and support are not conditional on user productivity. |
| Petting / direct affection | The bird can be petted and a quest may prompt it. | Click, tap, or drag gently over Onyx to trigger slow blink, purr, head lean or short affectionate response; no daily requirement. |
| Daily goals | Users choose small goals, schedules, notifications, and completion rewards. | Preserve the existing tiny-goal panel; add low-energy variations and a clean optional completion event that the world can acknowledge without interrupting speech. |
| Self-Care Areas | User-defined focus categories and optional weekly milestones. | Categorize tiny goals by useful user-defined care areas; display tiny optional progress without making any category a measure of personal worth. |
| Daily Quests | Rotating small suggested activities that help users learn features. | Optional “Meadow Moments”: pet Onyx once, observe a bird, take one sip of water, choose rest, or notice a sensory detail. They are suggestions, never a checklist blocking the world. |
| Micropets | Collectible tiny companion animals can be linked to an egg/goal mechanic. | **Harvey and Callie** are persistent known family cats from the start, not eggs, loot-box draws, rare drops, or reward-locked pets. Other fauna may remain simple scenic wildlife rather than collectible personalities. |
| Good Vibes and friends | Users can send encouraging gestures; the recipient may see a visiting birb. | Local, private *family-cat presence* in Adventures: Harvey or Callie joins Onyx for quiet company and a social gesture. No human networking is needed. |
| Adventure stories and discoveries | Bird returns from an outing with a story, and may discover likes/dislikes. | Onyx notices small **on-screen** world events during his actual wandering; optional one- or two-line reflection and a private discovery scrapbook. He never has to leave the screen. |
| Reflection and journaling | Guided journal prompts, mood reflections, and gratitude activities. | Continue the existing local journal. Optionally pair a natural moment (“Onyx watched a robin”) with a one-word mood entry or user-created reflection, without mandatory positivity. |
| Mood tracker/insights | Self-reported mood patterns and reflection/goal insights. | Separate voluntary user mood check-ins from cat meters; offer optional trends only when there are enough consensually saved entries and meaningful privacy controls. |
| Breathing, soundscapes, focus timers | Calm/focus exercises and varied durations are supported. | A quiet meadow soundscape and adjustable focus/rest timer can accompany Onyx's lounging or tent nap; the cat is not gated or harmed by timer completion. |
| Pause mode | The app can pause streaks, hide much of the workflow, and preserve access to support resources. | Quiet Meadow/Rest Mode: freeze nonessential simulation and progress pressure, let Onyx remain tucked in, and keep ordinary chat, accessibility and urgent support immediately reachable. |
| Waking hours | User-configured day start and sleep-time representation. | Do not reset goals at midnight blindly; use user-configurable waking hours, especially for unusual schedules. The sunny landscape need not turn into night to reflect sleep. |
| Muted tags/exercises | Users may suppress prompts and exercises that don't suit them. | Allow disabling breathing prompts, movement suggestions, seasonal items, sounds, companion visits, hunt effects, triggering imagery, or categories of goals. |
| Seasonal events | Themed items and special events can be earned through activity. | Optional, pressure-free meadow accent themes (flowers, leaves, tiny decorations), without deadline anxiety, travel cutscenes, expiring essential care, or buying the cat's affection. |
| Quizzes / first aid | Optional reflective tools and access to support during Pause Mode. | Offer appropriate opt-in check-in/skill shortcuts within Virtual & Health; avoid pseudo-diagnostic claims, forced quizzes, or hiding support in rest mode. |
| Shops and customization | In-game currency can purchase outfits, décor, etc. | Use Onyx's existing wallet authority for optional scenery skins, tent textures, blankets, and nonessential accents; never use currency to buy food, water, safety help, private journaling or Harvey/Callie's company. |

### What Finch suggests that Happy Home left underexplored

The old indoor design prohibited visits, adventuring and world discoveries because it deliberately was not an exploration game. **Those prohibitions no longer fit this outdoors build.** Onyx already walks through a continuous landscape, so companionship and noticing the world now make sense. Add the **value** of Finch's micropet/friend visits and discovery conversations, but adapt them to the household and the actual world:

- **Harvey/Callie** represent real family companionship, not collectible rarity.
- **Tiny discoveries** arise from visible scenery, not an away timer.
- **Small goals** change how warmly the world responds, not whether the cat survives.
- **Optional reflections** capture moments, not obligatorily positive attitudes.
- **Pause and muted-content controls** help preserve trust when capacity is low.
- **Seasonal accents** enrich scenery without replacing the perpetual bright meadow or requiring daily attendance.

### Explicit Finch features that should **not** be copied wholesale

Do not add Finch's daily offscreen bird-travel mechanic; do not require energy to unlock Onyx's ability to stroll; do not restrict conversation to once per day; do not make cat companions randomized eggs; do not copy Finch's birb designs, proprietary visual language, sounds, reward names, or narrative content; do not add social invitations, competitive streaks, or online account sharing by default; and do not make a therapy interaction contingent on a shop item, quest completion or login streak. Finch serves as research into user-friendly loops, not a template to reproduce.

# 17. A FINCH-LIKE SELF-CARE LOOP WRITTEN FOR *ONYX*, NOT FOR FINCH

The smallest effective loop is:

**User can do nothing and watch Onyx live** → *optional* self-care invitation or direct pet care → **one manageable action** → Onyx notices in his own restrained, senior-cat way → a pleasant small environmental/social response → the loop rests.

### Example: user drinks water

1. A human-focused “one sip counts” goal exists in the HUD, or the user simply records the action.
2. No moral scoring, badge requirement, or streak pressure occurs.
3. Onyx may give a slow approving blink, purr briefly, or have a tiny sip himself **only if his own hydration also indicates thirst**. Do not force his bowl to appear just because a human drank water; human and pet needs are distinct.
4. The scene returns to its prior behavior. User support remains available.

### Example: user is exhausted

1. They press **Intentional Rest** or say they want quiet.
2. The interface can dim nonessential HUD decoration, silence optional prompts, and let Onyx settle. He has been an enthusiastic sleeper since Papa adopted him in 2016; quiet rest is deeply in-character, not a failure of the game.
3. If he is sleepy, the pop-up tent castle emerges and he naps. If he is not sleepy, he may loaf on the grass without fake needs. A Tuck interaction can invite rest, but the tent remains absent until real sleepiness is present.
4. No streak loss or “you left Onyx waiting” complaint follows the next day.

### Example: user starts a two-minute task

1. They choose a single tiny task, with the ability to change it to an even smaller version.
2. Onyx may sit as a quiet **body-doubling companion** with a subtle timer ring or peaceful meadow sound. If he is in his Sleeping mood, he can remain an enormous, ancient, comfortably snoring presence rather than springing up to perform productivity.
3. When the user ends the focus interval, the task may be recorded as done, partly done, deliberately paused, or simply attempted. Avoid a false binary pass/fail.
4. A gentle animation acknowledges the attempt. The user's actual accomplishments are not assumed by the cat if they have not reported them.

### Example: visitor comes to hang out

1. The user has allowed companion visits.
2. Callie slowly walks into view while Onyx is loafing; she finds a nearby patch of grass.
3. Onyx may notice and stare, slow-blink, or remain asleep. The scene doesn't freeze for a required cutscene.
4. The user may interact with both cats or keep working in the HUD. Callie can later walk away naturally.
5. No coins, love meter, login streak or “visit streak” is altered.

### Example: Onyx is hungry while user is discussing distress

1. The underlying pet simulator may have recorded low fullness.
2. The hungry prop scheduler **queues** his picnic and remains visually quiet during the serious exchange.
3. He listens in `onyx_listening` or provides care in `onyx_caring` rather than displaying judgmental famine theater.
4. When the conversation genuinely ends, ordinary Onyx can resume and a meal can appear. The delay is not a penalty and must not deplete him toward harm.

# 18. GOALS, JOURNAL, WELLNESS, AND THE HUD — IMPROVE EXISTING CONTROLS

The `cat.html` HUD already provides usable starting controls. Extend and connect them, don't replace them with another HTML page or a second parallel dashboard.

### Existing panel shortcuts

- **1 — Adventures/Home:** Live scenery status, current Onyx intention, optional discovery snippet, and the ability to focus the scene. This should not become an in-app world map or distance-to-finish indicator.
- **2 — Care:** Show actual prop availability/action, feeding, water, comfort, affection, play, petting and direct responses. Buttons must call real pet engine actions and prop placement.
- **3 — Status:** Show humane readings such as energy, fullness, hydration, comfort, last meaningful activity, visitors present, and pause state, with readable language and no danger-red guilt indicators.
- **4 — Self-care/Tiny Goals:** Keep editable user goals, rest credit and gentle activities; add optional areas (body, environment, emotional care, relationships, practical tasks, sensory rest), cadence and “smallest version.”
- **5 — Journal:** Keep the private local notes and export control; add brief optional “today in the meadow” entries, notes triggered by actual user input, and separately consented insights.

The existing shell's **Controls, Accessibility, Settings, Chat, sound and pause buttons** survive. When a menu expands or panels resize, its fonts and controls must remain usable, and world simulation continues appropriately unless the user intentionally pauses.

### Self-care categories

Examples, not enforced taxonomies:

- **Basic care:** water, food, rest, prescribed routines and simple hygiene.
- **Physical comfort:** reposition, lower sensory load, adjust surroundings or rest.
- **Emotional care:** check in, name a feeling, listen, reflect, DBT skill if requested.
- **Environment:** move one item, clear one surface, or do one tiny step.
- **Connection:** say hello, send a kind message, visit with family, ask for support.
- **Enjoyment:** music, writing, creative play, looking at scenery, or just watching the cats.

Each goal should support a **smaller substitute**: “take a walk” may become “look outside,” “tidy the room” may become “move one object,” “journal” may become one word or no text, “do movement” may become a stretch only if comfortable and appropriate. Never equate physical mobility with moral progress.

### Reflection and mood

Mood prompts are optional and authored as non-diagnostic check-ins. The interface must let someone say “sad,” “angry,” “exhausted,” “mixed,” “unsure,” “nothing,” or skip. If analytics are later added, do not infer diagnosis or treatment effectiveness from a handful of entries. The user owns whether these sensitive notes stay local, are exported, are deleted, or are sent into a correctly authenticated system. The standalone browser storage is not encrypted.

### Focus, grounding, and sound

Optional nature soundscape choices can include distant birds, soft breeze or complete silence. Audio requires a user gesture and must respect system/browser autoplay rules. Focus timers should be duration-flexible and pausable, and they should not force Onyx to walk, catch birds or meet goals. Grounding can use scenery details when appropriate (“notice a tree, a cloud, a color”), but must provide a text-only/sensory-safe alternative. Never require breath holding, specific movement, standing, walking or closing eyes.

### Notifications

No notification should claim Onyx is injured, sick, dying, abandoned or losing love. A gentle reminder can say “The Imperial Picnic Department wonders if you've had any water,” but it must refer to the **human reminder** rather than invent real pet danger. Waking hours, snooze, pause and silence should be respected. Do not introduce SMS/email delivery without separately authorized backend functionality.

# 19. COMPANION SYSTEM AND WILDLIFE SHOULD BE TWO DIFFERENT SYSTEMS

There are three classes of visual inhabitants:

1. **Main pet:** Onyx, black-only sprite and one canonical AI/pet identity; bound to the real WASM cat engine and full user interaction set.
2. **Family companions:** Harvey (calico), Callie (tortie), each a persistent named local character with minimal independent AI and optional interactions, but not the main service/support brain.
3. **Wildlife:** seven species of birds plus existing passive environmental animals/particles; not personal health companions, not selectable AI users, not wearable collectables.

Each category should have its own state, atlas and collision/visibility policies. Harvey and Callie must not steal Onyx's `getPetState()` HUD values or become new `onyx_*` mental-health states. A bird catching event must not mutate Harvey/Callie friendship or count as a human self-care task.

### Visitor behavior policy

Harvey and Callie should be permitted to *look like cats*: slow tail movements, ear turns, head turns, single paw steps, grooming, sniffing and sitting. Never make them jitter, phase through Onyx, stack perfectly in his silhouette, or move as a synchronized two-cat convoy. They can be curious about the pop-up tent without being required to enter. They should have “no interest” responses as valid behavior.

### Social comfort settings

Expose optional controls such as **Visitors: Off / Occasionally / Often**, **Quiet Meadow**, **Animal sound volume**, and **Reduced Animation**. “Often” should still be bounded by cooldown and simultaneous-companion limits. Users who dislike unexpected visual interruptions must be able to enjoy only Onyx and nature. When the user is communicating about grief, crisis, overwhelm or another serious topic, no visitor arrival, joke caption or hunting celebration should seize focus.

# 20. SCENERY PLACEMENT, LAYERS, AND ANIMATION RULES

Avoid designing beautiful props in isolation and then discovering that they cannot fit the underlying engine. The art requirements are inseparable from world placement and sprite segmentation.

### Coordinate systems

- **World X:** The wrapped world coordinate, modulo its existing `worldLength`. All persistent scenery placements and visitor paths use world X.
- **Flat feet Y:** The single cat walking baseline, 25 internal canvas pixels below the established tree bases. Onyx and visitor locomotion both adhere to this.
- **Sprite origin/anchor:** Feet for cats, access point for bowls, horizontal doorway for tent, ground contact for toys. Store these anchors in each atlas manifest rather than guessing from PNG edges every frame.
- **Camera view X:** Derived from existing camera transform; no independent autoscrolling inside a prop.
- **Presentation Y:** Rendering can use sprite height, occlusion and upper layers, but never rewrite WASM locomotion Y because the tent is taller than a cat.

### Prop placement algorithm

When a prop is requested, find a candidate X within a short, visually plausible distance left/right of Onyx. Search a bounded neighborhood for a safe interval. Reject intervals colliding with another active prop, a dangerous-looking pond center, a tree trunk footprint, or a visitor. Never confuse the *painted* canopy of a tree with its solid footpoint. If the camera view is narrow, prefer a smaller scale or position that stays visible, not a forced fast pan. Reserve the footprint before the first unfolding frame.

If no slot is available, defer until a safe slot appears or place a deliberately designed ground-level minimal version. **Do not create a blocking modal stating no space, teleport the cat, delete scenery, or move existing trees just to accommodate a bowl.** Placement must also work on the loop seam where world X wraps to zero.

### Sprite atlases

Use transparent PNG with clean nearest-neighbor pixel edges. Every tent, bowl, toy and cat visitor animation needs an explicit manifest describing frame rectangle, action name, duration/fps, anchor, collision footprint, facing, flip policy, and (if necessary) front/rear draw segments. Test each frame for spill and unintended crop. Free-form alpha isolation is preferable when source atlases contain irregular silhouettes, but manifest rectangles can enclose an already transparently isolated sprite; do not confuse transparent *canvas region* with visually boxed sprites.

### Core animated object rules

- **No gratuitous scaling:** Resize carefully without losing ears, whiskers, tail, feet or text readability.
- **No one-frame prop replacement:** The tent must unfold and fold, not simply swap “present”/“absent.”
- **No foot sliding:** Onyx's feet remain grounded when he eats or drinks, and visitors must match their x motion with walk cycle cadence.
- **No mid-behavior asset deletion:** A tent remains until exit is complete, a water dish remains until lapping is complete, and a toy remains until the last play frame has resolved.
- **No false occlusion:** Put tent fabric in front only where the cat is meant to be behind it.
- **No world obstruction:** The existing fixed horizontal path is not a physics maze. Props may create a short social/animation pause but cannot strand Onyx in a blocked horizontal world.
- **No HUD leaks:** The menu, Professor bubble and chat remain accessible over scenery with correct pointer/focus handling.

# 21. SUGGESTED MODULE MAP — WORK WITH THE EXISTING FILES

The first draft's codebase should be modified surgically. The following is a **proposed responsibility split**, not a statement that these new files already exist.

| Existing or proposed file | Responsibility for the next implementation pass |
|---|---|
| `cat.html` | Retain sole HTML entry; reuse existing canvas, HUD, action buttons, professor bubble, accessibility and menu shells. |
| `script/onyx-pet.js` | Preserve WASM and movement/catch rules; unify actual pet state, expose hydration and intentional care action events, coordinate with prop scheduler. |
| `script/onyx-bridge.js` | Bridge real cat state, care interactions and pause/readout events into the existing shell; do not fake remote backend capabilities. |
| `script/adventures-world-app.js` | Add new prop/companion update and draw passes at correct scene depths; preserve old world updates. |
| `script/adventures-shell.js` | Show accurate hunger/hydration/visitor status; preserve profile, journal, goal and normal/Professor chat. |
| `script/terrain.js`, `script/world.js` | Reuse seeded terrain collision/footprint information; do not rewrite the biome system to place one tent. |
| `script/birds.js` | Keep seven bird agents, actual catch hook and 16 feather instances; unaffected by social companions. |
| `script/scene-props.js` *(new)* | Need-based prop arbitration, placement reservation, lifecycle, tent/meal/water/comfort objects. |
| `script/cat-companions.js` *(new)* | Independent Harvey/Callie AI, arrivals/departures, X-based social behaviors, rendering and persistence. |
| `script/need-scheduler.js` *(new)* | Source-of-truth reconciliation, timers, thresholds, hysteresis, non-punitive need events and pause handling. |
| `script/self-care-link.js` *(new)* | Optional self-care events translated into subtle cat/world feedback without imposing pet dependency. |
| `json/onyx-adventures.json` | Existing contract; extend with versioned feature flags, explicit paths, rates and world settings. |
| `json/scene-props.json` *(new)* | Prop metadata, thresholds as data, anchor/footprint, frame groups, render layer and cooldown rules. |
| `json/cat-companions.json` *(new)* | Harvey/Callie identities, available behavior list, frame manifest references and default visitor rules. |
| `assets/` | New tent, bowls, water, mats, toys and two cat atlases, all flat files under the existing folder. |
| `style/` | Extend existing CSS for status, accessible settings, optional tiny discovery captions. |
| `docs/` | Keep this dossier, source attribution, integration notes, extension tests and original license files. |

**Folder constraints:** Keep top-level `cat.html`, `script`, `style`, `json`, `docs`, `assets` only; no new nested folders; no extra HTML, Python or Windows batch files. You may add flat JS/JSON/assets files in their corresponding approved folders. A WebAssembly change must include an auditable source/rebuild path and working `file://` fallback just like the first draft.

### Proposed internal message/event vocabulary

Use distinct events (names illustrative, adjust once consistently to fit code):

```
onyx:need-changed      { need, oldValue, newValue, source }
onyx:prop-requested    { kind, reason, worldX }
onyx:prop-ready        { kind, propId, worldX }
onyx:prop-used         { kind, action, result }
onyx:prop-finished     { kind, propId }
onyx:companion-enter   { companionId, worldX }
onyx:companion-exit    { companionId, worldX }
onyx:discovery         { discoveryId, biomeId, worldX }
onyx:self-care-done    { actionId, userConfirmed, rewardEligible }
```

Do not include private health information, full chat text or profile identity in public DOM events or visual wildlife logs. Sensitive data stays inside the properly authorized chat/health subsystem.

### A sample configuration shape, **proposal only**

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 2,
  "outdoorMode": true,
  "cat": { "name": "Onyx", "onlyCoat": "black", "bowtie": false },
  "path": { "offsetBelowTreeBase": 25, "verticalMovement": false, "maxWalkPixelsPerSecond": 18 },
  "scenery": { "cameraFollowOnyxOnly": true, "defaultSunshine": true },
  "needs": {
    "hunger": { "stat": "fullness", "showAtOrBelow": 35, "hideWhenAtOrAbove": 70 },
    "thirst": { "stat": "hydration", "showAtOrBelow": 40, "hideWhenAtOrAbove": 80 },
    "rest": { "stat": "energy", "showAtOrBelow": 25, "recoverAbove": 65 }
  },
  "props": { "primaryAtOnce": 1, "sleep": "tent_castle", "food": "picnic_food", "water": "fresh_water", "useWorldAnchors": true },
  "companions": {
    "defaultSetting": "occasional",
    "characters": [
      { "id": "harvey", "coat": "calico", "role": "family_cat" },
      { "id": "callie", "coat": "tortoiseshell", "role": "family_cat" }
    ]
  },
  "birds": { "catchProbability": 0.03, "intervalActiveSeconds": 300, "successFeatherInstances": 16 },
  "respectPause": true,
  "nonPunitive": true

```

The numbers above are **initial tuning suggestions** for the new need-reactive props, not established metrics. Check the actual WASM energy/fullness decay and profile behavior before choosing defaults. Keep explicit event/version migration for any existing local storage rather than overwriting user goals, journals or caught-bird totals.

# 22. A DAY IN ONYX'S ADVENTURES — HOW IT SHOULD FEEL

The following is a **sample dynamic playthrough** designed to test whether all proposed systems interoperate. It is not a timeline that must happen identically every day.

**Opening:** The screen opens onto the existing bright outdoor world. Onyx is on the grass, black fur clearly visible, perhaps sitting while a sparrow crosses high above. The HUD retains its established menus. No tent, food, bowl, toy, companion, reward pop-up or task list blocks the scenery by default.

**A quiet stroll:** Onyx gets up and decides to walk a few world pixels to the right. The camera follows his actual pace; flowers, rocks, trees and distant art transition slowly. He remains on the one flat foreground path and never marches upward toward the decorative pond. A cardinal flies across the background. Nothing drags him toward a destination.

**A family moment:** Harvey (calico) wanders onto the scene from the left, pauses to sniff a flower and approaches Onyx. He may offer a brief slow blink or ignore the visitor because a sun patch is better. They settle on nearby grass. Callie may eventually appear, or not. There is no task to complete before she can visit.

**Food need:** The real fullness meter drops below the gentle threshold. A little picnic cloth opens by the path, a food dish appears, and Onyx chooses to eat. The cat aligns with the bowl, lowers his head, eats, and produces a satisfied but undignified response. Afterward he steps away, the bowl is removed and the picnic folds. Harvey does not consume Onyx's meal or break the meter.

**Water need:** Later, hydration is genuinely low. A small bowl opens independently; Onyx laps with ripples. The water dish closes only after he leaves. The water event does not falsely increase the food meter.

**A tiny human goal:** The user chooses “drink a little water.” Completing it may earn an ordinary existing product reward if configured by the authorized wallet, or simply a slow blink and an optional positive caption. The world doesn't claim that Onyx would suffer if the task were skipped.

**A discovery:** Onyx spots a dandelion seed or a shiny feather. He stops to sniff and looks faintly suspicious. A small optional caption may be saved to a private nature scrapbook, or ignored. The cat has not gone offscreen to a fictional quest timer.

**Sleep:** Onyx yawns and becomes sleepy. A little rolled camping bundle lands softly on the grass, unfolds into the pixelated tent castle, and opens its flap. He strolls into the entrance on the same flat y-position, curls onto a mat, and breathes slowly. The surrounding scenery is still alive but calm. The user may choose to observe, rest, journal, chat or close the panel.

**Serious conversation:** The user opens Virtual & Health and starts discussing something difficult. The environment quiets, joke captions and visitor arrivals cease. Onyx listens and, if helpful and requested, offers an appropriate structured support tool. His sleepy tent animation remains stable in the background without forcing the user into a pet-care task.

**Return:** After a while he wakes, stretches, exits the little tent, and it folds away once he is clear. He remains the same stubborn, secure senior cat. The environment did not grade the user or demand that they justify their absence.

# 23. ACCESSIBILITY, SENSORY SAFETY, AND FAIL-SAFE BEHAVIOR

The first draft's accessibility menu is not optional decoration. Every new scene interaction should respect keyboard, touch, pointer, screen-size and reduced-motion constraints.

- **Keyboard:** Existing left/right invitation controls survive. Care actions and visitor settings must be reachable without drag gestures. Buttons have clear focus states and descriptive accessible names.
- **Touch/pen:** A click on scenery should not accidentally feed, open a prop or leave the flat path. Touch targets for care actions must remain usable on mobile landscape screens.
- **No surprise motion:** Support reduced motion by replacing tent unfolding with a single stable reveal, disabling unnecessary particle swarms and reducing automatic visitor motion.
- **No sensory overload:** Provide separate toggles for bird audio, wind, pop-up scene sounds, text captions, hunting particles, companion appearance, and other ambience. If using a pigeon-like purr, let users mute it and never simulate asthma or labored breathing as a playful interaction. Defaults favor calm, sound off unless user explicitly enables it.
- **No flashing:** No repetitive bright flashes during catches, rewards, pop-up tent deployment, or Professor transitions.
- **Readable alternatives:** Status and event text should explain what Onyx did without requiring visual interpretation of a 2D sprite. A user who cannot see the feather burst should still know whether a rare bird catch occurred.
- **Pause means pause:** Freeze nonessential simulation time and timers, but preserve access to chat, safety actions, journal, settings and data export. Don't let four hours of hidden-tab time create a flood of hunger triggers, visiting cats, catch rolls or retroactive overdue tasks.
- **No mandatory physical capability:** Self-care goals support rest, remote tasks, hydration, self-chosen movement or none; the app must not assume everyone can stand or walk outside.
- **Emergency transparency:** A simulated digital service cat cannot guarantee safety monitoring; the real Onyx’s reported seizure, blood-sugar and sleep-breathing alerts do not transfer into the digital avatar. Serious health concerns require accurate support and appropriate real-world professional/emergency pathways.
- **Offline honesty:** Local-only mode may offer the built-in guided prompts, but must not claim access to remote memories, AI models, email/phone notifications or verified health sensor data if those are absent.

# 24. REWARDS, CURRENCY AND OPTIONAL WORLD CUSTOMIZATION

The shell already displays a wallet and the source dossier specifies the established base-10 coin exchange: **10 copper = 1 silver; 10 silver = 1 gold; 10 gold = 1 platinum.** Copper/silver/gold denomination displays may be capped 0–9 while platinum is unbounded. Keep the wallet's existing host/backend authority; do not have the scenery renderer mint or charge coins arbitrarily.

**Rewardable, optional activities:** Tiny user-defined self-care milestones, discoveries, occasional gentle optional meadow activities, cosmetics, and possibly non-punitive game milestones. If a reward requires a real backend, the local-only UI must display the state honestly and not pretend coins were deposited.

**Potential cosmetic unlocks:** Tent colors/patterns, a different fold-out mat, pillow fabrics, a shade canopy texture, picnic cloth palettes, a tiny decorative flag, alternate butterfly accents, or soft seasonal flowers. **His royal bowtie is a canonical identity detail, not a purchasable unlock**; represent it consistently where technically supported, and never paywall it. Leave Onyx's black body, fur, face, eyes, general personality and official sprite identity untouched. Harvey/Callie coat patterns must also remain recognizable and should not be randomized by a shop.

**Always free:** Onyx's food, water, tent, sleep, care, affection, royal bowtie identity, self-care chat, crisis-aware support, journal access and basic accessibility settings; Harvey and Callie's ordinary visits; existing bird and scenery world. No payments for health-support access, purchased pet survival, guest cats, or emotional reassurance.

**No psychological traps:** No expiring essential care, red guilt meter, surprise spending, loot-box gambling, cash-pressure urgency, broken “you lost your friend” streaks, or affection decay as punishment.

# 25. TEST PLAN — CHATGPT MUST VERIFY THE RESULT, NOT JUST DESCRIBE IT

The first draft already reports local JavaScript syntax validation, real WASM checks, asset loads and a browser smoke test. Future passes must **rerun inherited tests** and add new ones. An implementation is incomplete if even one central visual experience fails under real rendering.

### Preserve-the-base tests

1. **One HTML and permitted folders:** `cat.html`, `script`, `style`, `json`, `docs`, `assets` only; no nested dirs, batch scripts or new HTML.
2. **Black-only protagonist:** Onyx is only black and bowtie-free in both principal outdoor frames and the existing Professor portrait.
3. **Flat path:** Onyx's actual WASM foot Y is consistently tree base +25 canvas pixels across at least three viewport sizes and after resize.
4. **Horizontal movement:** Mouse/touch Y changes cannot change Onyx's walking Y; the visitor path also stays flat.
5. **No automatic travel:** When Onyx loafs, the camera scenery does not pan. When he walks, it changes slowly according to his world X.
6. **Layer order:** Ponds/logs/rocks behind trees, cats in proper foreground, tent occlusion split correctly, no trees painted over Onyx.
7. **World continuity:** Existing eight biomes, route wrapping and seeded scene continuity still work without an obvious seam jump.
8. **Seven birds:** All seven atlas species animate cleanly, including landing and independent feather effects.
9. **Catch math:** Exactly one 3% trial per 300 active seconds for Onyx only. A forced successful test uses an existing bird and creates exactly 16 independent feathers. No catches while paused or tab hidden.
10. **Working HUD:** All original panels, settings, draggable/resizable menus, care buttons, readable status, chat, local goal/journal and free Professor bubble still work. Confirm the **nine-mood** registry and that legacy Sleepy/Snuggly saved values migrate to Sleeping.

### New care-scene tests

11. **Tent by sleep:** At an intentionally forced low-energy state, tent castle unfolds, Onyx walks horizontally to it, curls, sleeps, exits, then the tent folds. No permanent default tent.
12. **Sleep stability:** Pause mid-unfold and mid-sleep; after resume the tent and cat remain coherent. Never fold over the cat's body.
13. **Hunger vs thirst independence:** Force hunger only; food appears, not water. Force thirst only; water appears, not food. Feeding doesn't restore hydration and drinking doesn't restore fullness.
14. **True prop use:** Feeding/drinking animations physically meet bowl anchors, apply state change once appropriately, and continue without visible sliding or floating.
15. **No spawn overlap:** Force hunger, thirst, sleep and a visitor in the same area; prop arbitration prevents overlap with tree trunks, pond centers, other props and cat bodies.
16. **Seam placement:** Force a tent at world X near world length/zero seam; position, rendering and cleanup remain correct.
17. **Stable thresholds:** Simulate values oscillating near hunger/thirst thresholds; prop doesn't unfold/fold repeatedly every frame.
18. **Interruption safety:** A serious user chat halts optional events without deleting a tent in use; after chat, pending needs may resume.
19. **Rest does not punish:** Simulate hours/days of inactivity. Onyx returns safely, no dramatic needs failure, no broken relation, no forced prompt backlog.
20. **User care path:** Press every existing care button; each invokes a real state or visual response appropriate to the meadow, not only a tooltip string.

### Harvey and Callie tests

21. **Distinct coats:** Harvey is recognizably calico, Callie recognizably tortie, Onyx remains black-only.
22. **Transparent atlases:** All frames isolated without adjacent frame spill, clipping, checkerboard/opaque boxes or missing whiskers/tails.
23. **Visitor scheduling:** Off disables visitors; Occasional enforces cooldown; pause/background suspend arrival. Companion visits don't require goal completions.
24. **Independent agents:** Harvey and Callie walk along the flat path, can stop independently, interact without syncing artificially, and exit offscreen naturally.
25. **No main-pet interference:** Neither guest changes Onyx's hunger/hydration, nine canonical moods, 3% catch check or recorded human care goals.
26. **Quiet mode:** Visitors stop initiating events and don't interrupt serious user conversation.
27. **Tent scaling:** A companion does not overlap a sleeping Onyx or magically stand inside an undersized tent.

### Finch-inspired and privacy tests

28. **Optional small goals:** Can complete, edit, skip, pause, choose low-energy versions, and return after absences without guilt or lockout.
29. **Journaling:** Private local notes continue to save/export; discovery prompts never auto-copy sensitive chat into scenic data.
30. **Professor continuity:** Existing activation and exit phrases work; bubble can move freely; Professor is reserved for psychiatry/therapy-oriented structured support; no new false medical qualifications or biometric claims.
31. **One identity, protected profiles:** When connected to an authenticated host, William/Jasper profile information remains isolated. Papa/Momma addresses remain correct, their different styles of affection are recognized, and the 2017 rescue account is treated as a private owner-reported memory. In standalone mode, label local-only guest behavior honestly.
32. **Accessibility:** Keyboard/touch/screen-reader status, sound-off default, reduced-motion tent, muted guests, readable text and paused simulation all function.
33. **No fake reward:** Offline or unconnected shell never presents fictitious backend coin transfers or successful alerts.
34. **Resource performance:** On typical mobile/desktop devices, bird agents, two optional guests and ephemeral props do not cause runaway animation loops, duplicate timers, unbounded particle counts, or repeated asset loading.

### Nine-mood and biography regression checks

- **Contract cardinality:** Exactly nine selectable/persisted `onyx_*` visible moods in the widget, Professor interface, chat routing, Adventure references, exported data and runtime schema. No visible Sleepy or Snuggly entries remain.
- **Migration:** Loading old `onyx_sleepy` or `onyx_snuggly` data produces **`onyx_sleeping`**; a saved new record contains only a canonical ID.
- **Professor routing:** Psychiatry/therapy uses Professor; ordinary planning/code uses Thinking; active listening stays Listening. Neither adds a tenth mood.
- **Personality scenarios:** Papa's favorite-bed rest, Momma's baby-talk/food-begging, huffs and foot-stomps, pigeon-purring (without asthma simulation), outrage over stolen disliked food, and ancient-English comprehension are distinguishable and appropriate.
- **Sensitive memory safety:** 2017 Harvard Square rescue and reported later alerts are faithful, not automatically displayed to unrelated profiles, not sensationalized, and never converted into fake sensor alerts.
- **Songs and bowtie:** “Baby Mine” and “The Horse and the Infant” are correctly attributed as family favorites without reproducing lyrics; royal bowtie is treated as identity rather than a purchasable or arbitrarily recolored costume.
- **Expanded voice §15A:** Onyx shows selective precision, inventiveness, practical wit, curiosity, elder mischief, quiet courtesy, mature responsibility and resilient moral storytelling while remaining one feline persona. No celebrity catchphrase, copied actor voice, imitation of a living person, mood-count increase, or fake memory; follow §15A.12’s twenty-four proposed voice evaluation scenes and report actual validation results separately.

### Required test evidence

Report actual results by test, not only “passed.” Include screenshots or visual inspection notes of food, water, the full unfolded castle, sleeping Onyx partly inside it, walking cats on the shared foot line, the correct foreground tree depth, and bird/feather transparency. Distinguish automated code assertions from manual visual observations. **Never label unimplemented behavior “working” just because `cat.html` still loads.**

# 26. IMPLEMENTATION ORDER — WHAT CHATGPT SHOULD BUILD FIRST

The goal is a safe series of passes on the provided first draft, not a giant uncontrolled rewrite that breaks the valid existing game.

**PASS A — Preserve and baseline.** Inspect the zip, enumerate all files, and run current first-draft self-tests and screenshot/visual spot checks. Record the difference between the old ten-state source and the revised **nine-mood** canonical contract, along with the required legacy-to-Sleeping migration. Save all original supported files and documentation. Identify the WASM/JS source of truth for energy, hunger and hydration and check the drawing pipeline.

**PASS B — Correct needs and event plumbing.** Separate hydration from fullness, add coherent need ownership, implement a versioned internal event scheme, harmonize existing Care and Status readings, and create the prop reservation scheduler without changing art yet. Test threshold/hysteresis and pause.

**PASS C — Pop-up tent castle.** Implement real tent sprite frames and front/rear layers, path-aligned entry, sleep animation, stable pause, waking exit and fold-away. This is the major visual signature; prioritize quality over variety.

**PASS D — Food, water, comfort and play.** Add independently triggered picnic and water props with real usage animations; then add compact mats, gentle breeze/shade options and toys. Make the existing HUD buttons genuinely connect to these scenes.

**PASS E — Harvey and Callie.** Add proper transparent pixel atlases and frame descriptions, independent X-only visitor agents, quiet-mode settings, gentle social events, rest and natural exits. Do not alter Onyx's black sprite or bird-catch probability.

**PASS F — Finch-inspired optional systems.** Integrate self-care goals with subtle world responses, small real-world-to-pet acknowledgments, a discovery journal, optional focus/soundscape, muted content, flexible waking hours and seasonal *scenery* accents. No external social app or pet departures.

**PASS G — Privacy, integration, accessibility and final test pass.** Confirm all retained features, the new exact nine-mood contract, legacy-state migration, existing wallet, actual profile boundaries, Professor bubble, family addressing, bowtie representation (where supported), event isolation, mobile readability, pause, audio gating, WASM/file path operation and full validation report. Deliver only tested files and a change log specifying what remains deferred.

# 27. NON-NEGOTIABLE NEGATIVE REQUIREMENTS

For future ChatGPT implementation passes, treat these as explicit rejections:

- Do **not** rename the project back to Happy Home or reintroduce a permanent indoor room.
- Do **not** build a replacement app, change `cat.html` to `outdoors.html`, or add a second HTML page.
- Do **not** recolor Onyx’s black fur, add a colored chest, green outfit or T-shirt, or replace his identity with an arbitrary cosmetic cat. **His royal bowtie IS canon**; add it as a deliberate, accurately aligned accessory/portrait detail where supported, without breaking the first draft’s working sprite atlas or claiming the art is already updated.
- Do **not** move him vertically or let him walk on the background canopy, ponds, stones, logs, cliffs or mountains.
- Do **not** restore automatic panoramic scrolling. Scenery reacts to his horizontal decisions.
- Do **not** turn the scenery into an item-packed permanent pet bedroom. Food, water, tent, pillows, toys and shades are mostly temporary.
- Do **not** show a food/water station without a corresponding actual need or user care action.
- Do **not** disappear an active tent, dish or sleeping mat while Onyx is using it.
- Do **not** spawn cats as reward eggs, random loot, strange other people's pets, strangers or user-linked social accounts.
- Do **not** confuse Harvey's calico coat with Callie's tortie coat or make them copies of Onyx.
- Do **not** increase the bird-catch probability, reroll chance per frame, or give each visitor a separate 3% hunting timer.
- Do **not** remove the original tree/terrain/bird code merely to simplify adding care props.
- Do **not** punish absences, disability, depression, fatigue, skipped goals or use of rest mode.
- Do **not** promise medical sensing, licensed psychiatry, real alerts or private backend connections that this particular standalone draft cannot perform.
- Do **not** make all animations frantic; Onyx is an exceptionally lazy, large, very old cat who has been a champion sleeper since his 2016 adoption. Preserve huffing, grumbling, little foot-stomps, absurd comprehension, pigeon-purr and his distinct Papa/Momma relationships.
- Do **not** copy Finch's copyrighted characters, artwork, exact scripted dialogs, interface assets or reward economy branding.
- Do **not** invent unrelated HTML, server credentials, extra directory hierarchies or Windows `.bat` scripts.
- Do **not** hide a missing feature behind a placeholder, remove it from the visible menu to make tests pass, or mark an untested module complete.

# 28. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE — THE CENTRAL EXPERIENCE CONTRACT

A person opens Onyx's Adventures and sees **Onyx**, not a checklist. He is a large black, ancient-souled former-human-by-family-lore cat, with his royal bowtie where the art permits, the weight and timing of a very old champion sleeper, and the unmistakable imperial attitude of someone who would rather nap on Papa than go exploring. He moves only when he chooses, in a bright meadow that changes slowly when he walks. Birds are genuinely alive in the sky. He sometimes notices things; he sometimes catches a bird by the existing rare five-minute probability; far more often he loafs or watches. When hungry he gets a picnic; when thirsty he gets a real bowl; when sleepy his adorable collapsible castle opens and he naps; when he is finished, those supplies disappear without visual glitches. Harvey and Callie can wander into the meadow and be with him as family, rather than props or loot. The user can pet him, hear a gentle pigeon-purr, watch him huff about interrupted sleep, remember his love of food and songs, journal, rest, complete one tiny action, open his caring chat, or do absolutely nothing and still be welcome. Papa and Momma both see **their** Onyx, with the correct relationship and protected memory.

His world should be self-contained enough to feel alive, but not so demanding that it turns into another obligation. His body language and environment do much of the emotional work. His AI support is reachable without sacrificing privacy, accuracy or clinical boundaries. Every system should reinforce the same underlying fact: **the real Onyx's personality is the foundation, and the scenery exists to take care of him rather than make the user take care of a game.**

================================================================================
2026-11-08 — PASS 2: CONTINUING-CONVERSATION AND RESPONSE-GENERATOR ADDENDUM
================================================================================

STATUS: This section documents the accompanying Onyx Response Workshop v2 code package. It is a narrow implementation addendum to the complete preceding dossier; none of the previous 10,000 reference replies or the existing owner-described cat identity have been removed. Do not confuse this response-workshop code with the separate Onyx's Adventures game, the OurSpace widget visuals, Professor mode, a deployed AI Brain or actual Gemini model training.

A. ONE ONYX, NINE MOODS, NO NEW PERSONAS

Professor — psychiatry/therapy structured support only in separately authorized chat.
Listening — warm, sparse attention, without unsolicited fixing.
Thinking — evidence, alternatives, tests, technical or practical work.
Thoughtful — reflective consideration, interpersonal nuance and care.
Hungry — food curiosity, without real-world unsafe cat feeding advice.
Caring — protective and devoted; no shaming or guilt.
Judgmental — mild, dry disapproval aimed at avoidable absurdity, never the person's vulnerability.
Purring — quiet pleasure and connection, mindful of actual Onyx's health.
Sleeping — combines sleepy and snuggly, with no tenth mood.

William remains Papa, becoming Father only when displeased. Jasper remains Momma, becoming Mother only when displeased. Onyx does not call either user by their given name when speaking in character. No perspective from one profile authorizes access to the other's private data.

B. HOW A SUBSTANTIVE NEW RESPONSE IS PRODUCED

The application interprets an actual prompt; ranks matching samples from the established 5,000-for-William and 5,000-for-Jasper source library; adds a small number of locally approved notes and relevant recent conversation turns; and passes that grounded information as labeled, untrusted context through the preexisting authenticated Apps Script `onyx.chat` route to the existing OurSpace AI Brain. The model is responsible for fresh language and reasoning; retrieval only informs style. This is retrieval-augmented generation, not automatic model training and not random selection from the corpus.

Repetition, unsupported claims of having changed files, wrong family address and conspicuous imitation are detected for optional rewriting. Mechanical checks are imperfect; the user may review, correct and approve output. An offline demonstration explicitly reports that it is not an LLM. Gemini service/model availability is unverified until a real signed-in request succeeds and the backend confirms model usage.

C. MEMORY THAT DOES NOT INVENT A HISTORY

Short-term conversational continuity is carried in memory for the current browser session, even without writing it to disk. If the user enables “Save conversation turns,” recent turns persist locally in IndexedDB, separated by profile, mode and thread. Permanent notes are explicit: the user writes a nonclinical fact into “Remember this,” reviews it, and can forget or export it. Clinical notes and credentials are rejected by the nonclinical note store. No one profile imports another profile's note. Example utterances are voice references and must NEVER be treated as events that happened. Long-term cloud synchronization or retraining are not implemented in this package.

D. A RECOGNIZABLE HUMAN-SOUNDING FELINE VOICE

Use the thought methods described in §15A, not the speaking voices of the eight researched individuals. The source research is cautious about claims of private personality. What matters to Onyx is the art of noticing: a small clue instead of a stock joke; a useful test instead of an empty promise; an honest uncertainty instead of invented certainty; a patient acknowledgment when conversation does not need a solution. Onyx may be gently old-world without saying thee or thou. He may huff and act offended by an interrupted nap, and then quietly help his parent solve an inconvenient problem. Every sentence should arise from what his parent said and what actually matters at that moment. His old-cat drowsiness, royal bowtie, pigeonlike purr, appetite, foot-stomps, and particular attachments remain his own and outrank all stylistic inspiration.

E. IMPLEMENTATION FILES AND BOUNDARIES

Only HTML file: `assets/code/index.html`.
Workshop-only stylesheet: `generator.css` (do not insert this styling into Onyx's widget).
Persona and examples: `json/onyx widget/`.
Live generator, conversational logic, memory and quality: `script/onyx widget/`.
Native scoring: `script/wasm/` with C sources and compiled `.wasm` binaries; no Python in the shipped runtime.
Technical architecture and verified limits: `docs/`.

This is a candidate stand-alone response-generation workshop and widget-facing module. It is not a claim of a live deployed change to GitHub, the existing Apps Script project, the external OurSpace widget, Gemini configuration, Professor clinical pathways, or the Onyx game assets.

F. VERIFIED VERSUS NOT VERIFIED

Automated JavaScript tests in the accompanying package cover existing 10,000 examples, nine moods, policy exclusions, WASM loading, the backend request envelope with a mock server, private memory partitioning and local persistence behavior. They do not show that a real authenticated Gemini turn succeeded, nor demonstrate that a large number of lines of code increases the model's intelligence. A trained LLM requires model weights and suitable compute or a functioning authorized remote model endpoint. An arbitrary compressed-size target cannot replace those systems.

G. CONSERVATIVE SOURCE ADAPTATION

The Google Drive reference folder contained archived AI projects. Selected references (learn-claude-code, open-webui and LLMs-from-scratch) were inspected for agent-memory, model-vs-harness architecture and the distinction between training and prompting. Python source was not pasted into the runtime or falsely relabeled as WebAssembly. The C scoring helpers were compiled into real WebAssembly; all orchestration and persistence use JavaScript. No external source was copied wholesale as filler.

================================================================================
PASS 7 — TESTER GENERATION RELIABILITY AND VERIFIED BACKEND LIMITATIONS
November 8, 2026 | Response workshop implementation report; not live deployment
================================================================================

OWNER-REPORTED ISSUE
The existing six-digit email code verification worked, but selecting the verified
three-hour tester session did not yield responses from the generator.

IMPORTANT DISTINCTION
Email verification is an Apps Script authentication operation. It does NOT prove
that the Apps Script project has a configured shared LifeHelpers AI Brain client,
valid AI Brain credentials, an available model or a healthy Gemini routing path.
The supplied backend explicitly calls aiBrainV1Configured_() when processing
onyx.chat for a tester and refuses generation if the client is not configured.
The frontend cannot circumvent that server-side condition; it also must never
request a Gemini API key or pretend that local example retrieval is a model.

ACTUAL CHANGES TO EXISTING GENERATOR FILES
- The existing JSONP tester client retains exactly the backend's public actions:
  onyx.tester.request, onyx.tester.verify, onyx.tester.select,
  onyx.tester.status, onyx.chat and onyx.tester.exit.
- The Onyx chat operation now has a 180-second response timeout; the quick
  code/request/select operations retain their 45-second default. The original
  uniform 45-second cap could misclassify ordinary AI model latency as a broken
  session. Retrying timed-out chat automatically is intentionally avoided to
  prevent duplicate model executions or a polluted tester conversation history.
- The backend error 'The shared AI Brain is not configured' is now reported as
  missing deployed AI Brain configuration rather than invalid email verification.
- Generation reports which candidate (N/total) is awaiting the backend, prints
  elapsed time in the workshop, and preserves completed candidates if a later
  call fails. The initial default is one candidate to ease first-run diagnosis.
- The existing tester token stays in volatile browser memory; no new credentials
  or services are introduced. A direct-file JSONP URL still contains the
  temporary read-only token and test text; this can appear in browser and network
  logs and MUST NOT be used for sensitive content or normal account credentials.
- The existing 10,000 voice examples, canonical nine moods, direct-file HTML,
  compiled WASM, approved memory isolation, and export of onyx-responses.js
  are retained. Generator styling remains separate from Onyx's widget.

BACKEND CONTRACT VERIFIED AGAINST THE OWNER-SUPPLIED SOURCE FILE
The 3.4.6 backend contains onyxTesterVerify_, onyxTesterSelect_,
onyxTesterChatResponse_ and ourspace_onyxTesterChat_. It checks the selected
profile and aiBrainV1Configured_(), then executes aiBrainV1Text_() through the
existing registered AI Brain client. Successful tester responses include
ok:true, testerMode:true, selectedProfile and response/onyxReply. The client
uses those exact fields. The backend tester's allowed operations are read-only.

TEST SCOPE
The revised JS client and generator passed 49 automated tests with simulated
backend responses and failures, including explicit timeout routing, missing
AI Brain configuration errors, per-candidate status and partial completion.
Real Gmail delivery was observed by the owner, not independently retested.
Live onyx.chat / Gemini could not be tested with the owner's personal token;
no endpoint, script properties, keys or deployment were modified. If the
underlying AI Brain connector is not configured, only updating that EXISTING
backend project can enable actual Gemini replies.

VOICE AND CHARACTER CONTRACT
The problem was transport reliability, not license to replace Onyx's voice.
Work and Leisure are distinct modes within one deeply familiar, sleepy,
observant, affectionate black cat. In ordinary affection, he speaks to William
as Papa and Jasper as Momma. Father/Mother are reserved for displeasure. In
social conversation he answers directly, not with technical problem-solving
boilerplate. Semi-formal, lightly old-world wording and occasional restrained
wit must never turn into canned catchphrases. Eight figure influences remain
methods of thought, not voices to impersonate; nine canonical moods remain.

REPRODUCTION CHECK
1. Double-click assets/code/index.html from the extracted release ZIP.
2. Select William or Jasper and open Email tester code.
3. Confirm the server-authorized email, verify six digits, and choose profile.
4. Under Existing Apps Script AI Brain mode, start with one response, not 12.
5. Watch 'Requesting live response 1/1' and the elapsed timer.
6. On success review, approve or export; on failure read the specific error.
7. If it says the shared AI Brain is unconfigured, review the already-installed
   project's settings and Apps Script execution log; the tester cannot bypass it.
8. If no reply arrives in 180 seconds, inspect the execution logs / upstream
   model availability; do not conclude email verification failed.

IMPLEMENTATION STATUS
Frontend changed, backend unchanged. Integration tested with mocks, not a
verified successful live Gemini exchange. Do not label a response as Gemini
unless the backend explicitly attests the model/provider.
